preview: An interview experience at BNY Mellon for a 2023 Summer Internship covering online assessment, multiple technical interview rounds involving DSA, OOPS, DBMS, OS, and projects.
content: BNY Mellon Interview Experience Shubham Salunkhe | TY B.Tech CS 2020-2024 For 2023 Summer Internship (On-campus) DSA Coding Round : 06/08/2022, 6.30pm BNYM Coding Test Round 1 : 08/08/2022, 7pm 25 candidates were selected for Round 1 after the coding round Projects and describe yourself I told about myself and what courses I had taken and about my project. In my android app development project, me and my team had developed a meme generator and while I was explaining one of its features, Interviewer interrupted me and asked why I had used a cloud platform to store the uploaded memes where I could have also be able to implement it by using a stand alone server? Oops what is abstraction and its implementation in c++ on given code pair link from hackerrank So I implemented a base class and derived class, where the base class had a virtual function which makes it abstract and I override that function in the derived class. Interviewer followed it up by asking what difference does virtual keyword make. So, I created a base class pointer and showed that if we had used virtual keyword then a base class pointer pointing to a derived class object, it will display overridden function but without virtual keyword in base class pointer will display function of base class only even if it is pointing to a derived class object. What is inheritance and how is it useful? I explained inheritance and gave an example of class person(with aadhar card no.) can be inherited to create classes like student(with aadhar card no. and reg.ID) and employee class(with aadhar card no. and employee ID) Dbms ddl, dml Truncate, delete (don’t just give the most obvious and common answer of delete command goes one by one but truncate deletes all at once; also some other points like delete command will give rise to a trigger but truncate would not) Follow up question “I run statement – delete * table_name; will it delete rows one by one or all at once. I replied in the log it will delete rows one by one but for the user it will appear all the rows have been deleted at once. And how will you scale your application so that many users can use it? Suppose the application and server can handle 1,000 users at a time, you want to scale it to 10,000. How will you do it? I said things like we can manage network traffic, increase the capacity of our server. She told me that I was on the right track and asked me “how will you “scale” your application. Does something strike your mind ?” I thought for some time and I said no ma’am I don’t know. She said it's okay But I asked her out of curiosity that how are we going to achieve this she instructed me to go through “Horizontal and Vertical Scaling” Round 2 : 09/08/2022, 12pm 11 candidates were selected for the 2nd Round after the 1st Round. And Finally 6 candidates were selected for the Internship. At the very start of Interview he asked me “how was my life going etc?” Express yourself freely and if asked about your daily life just tell them that I told him I did Android dev in sem3 Then in sem4 I completed NPTEL’s AI course And learnt basics of machine learning, I also told him about why I was fascinated by MLl, because at the heart of it it is math eg backprop mai you have chain rule as basic He asked me what's going in life I literally told him what's happening in my life I shared the dilemma that we as flight software Subsystem(Satellite Team of Vishwa) faced after the meet with expert on Sunday (07/08/2022) I also shared him about my hobby as theater acting and my experience with Natyavardhan I told him that while I was practicing or acting, I felt relaxed and I also got a chance to be creative as we had to do numerous improvisations. He replied that yes it very important to have a hobby or other thing will makes you relaxed DSA I was asked 2 dsa questions BNYM Round 2 DSA Qs And in the first question because I used STL sort, he asked me what algorithm does stl uses from inside => I said maybe merge sort or quicksort And then we had a discussion about merge sort and quicksort and comparisons between them. He asked me which is better? => I said if we consider the worst case merge sort is better because it has nlogn time complexity while the worst case of quicksort is n^2. But when the average case is considered both of them perform equally good but quicksort is used more often in real applications. For the second question I had explained the logic on the white board and he seemed to be satisfied with it. I think I had executed it properly but it did not pass all cases and the Interviewer informed me that they were having some issues with their compiler, so nothing to worry about. OS What are threads? Do you know about multi threading? How will you avoid deadlock? I was able to answer all these smoothly. What algorithm will you use to decrypt a secret message when you know the hash value of the original message? I tried thinking for some time but I said I don’t have any idea about it. So he asked me to explain Encryption and decryption I was able to explain it and why it is important Then he asked me about https I replied with its full form and mentioned that s represents that the website is secure. So he followed it up by asking what conditions should to be satisfied to so that the website can be called secure I was unable to answer and I mentioned that I have not been taught Computer Networks in my college yet OOPS I was asked “give a brief explanation about all of the OOPS concepts that you know” So I first explained 4 pillars of OOPS and then stated subtopics of each of the 4. I followed this by giving one liner explanations of all subtopics like various types of inheritance; compile time polymorphism with eg of function and operator overloading; runtime polymorphism with eg of function overriding; abstraction and virtual functions and their uses; At the end of the interview, I was asked Why do you want to code? I shared my experience while developing my app and how we would take hours to debug but at the end of the day when debugging was completed we would emerge out with some learning.I gave example that I would make global variable of user object to access user in different classes and files and that would most of the time fail; later we got to know there is a function provided by firebase auth that would give us userID directly.(give examples from your project, jo bhi bolte bolte yaad aajaye voh bolo). I also said “Yeah I love problem solving and logic building but along with that I also like coding because while coding/debugging we keep learning new things” Why BNY Mellon for internship? I had attended the offline PrePlacement Talk and honestly I was really very thankful that they organized it offline because I got to know about what finances/business they actually do and why they need technology. I mentioned that and thanked them about it. BNY Mellon being a big corporation I would get good exposure to new and interesting technologies mentioned during ppt like NLP, ML, payments software, IOT, etc. RESOURCES DSA 1. Striver SDE sheet 2. Code help(love babbar's 2nd channel) for some concepts after completing topics from sde sheet I would go and see what all other questions he has taken in his DSA playlist (this helped me largely in topics like hash maps, stack, queue and heap 3. Striver Recursion, Trees, graph and DP series really help me make these concepts strong (but to make graphs good enough also go through love babbar sheet questions of graph) OOPS 1. Use below link to revise OOPS concepts https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/ 2. If you are not comfortable with some concepts, I highly recommend to have a good understanding of all of the concepts first because OOPs was pressed upon in both the rounds(like I was not very comfortable with virtual functions so I had watched a video of Code with Harry about the same while revising OOPS) DBMS I revised most of the dbms concepts through Shraddha ma'am's slides Understood b and b+ trees from gate smashers You can refer gate smashers for understanding DBMS concepts For revision go through this : https://takeuforward.org/interviews/must-do-questions-for-dbms-cn-os-interviews-sde- core-sheet/ OS You can refer gate smashers for understanding OS concepts For revision go through this : https://takeuforward.org/operating-system/most-asked-operating-system-interview-que stions/ CN I just told the interviewer that we have not been taught Computer Networks yet in your syllabus. *****ALL THE BEST*****
